facts.raw_span: a 3-month history of rapidly spreading intensively pruritic papules on her extremities
no remarkable medical or family history
not concurrently being treated with any medications
scattered, erythematous, annular papules measuring up to 5 mm wide
a few asymptomatic brown flat papules scattered on her face
the palms, soles, and oral mucosa were not involved
Routine blood, liver and kidney function, antistreptolysin O, C-reactive protein, antinuclear antibody, and rheumatoid factor tests disclosed no abnormal findings
Mild hyperkeratosis accompanied by parakeratosis
Atrophy of the epidermis
Well-developed cornoid lamellae with a decreased granular layer
Individual cell dyskeratosis
Slight infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and eosinophils in the upper dermis

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of pruritic papules and the histopathology findings of mild hyperkeratosis, atrophy of the epidermis, and individual cell dyskeratosis are consistent with Grover's disease.
The patient's symptoms of pruritic papules and the histopathology findings of mild hyperkeratosis and atrophy of the epidermis are consistent with Darier's disease.
The patient's symptoms of pruritic papules and the presence of asymptomatic brown flat papules are consistent with Pityriasis rubra pilaris.
The patient's symptoms of pruritic papules and the histopathology findings of a slight infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and eosinophils are consistent with Lichen planus.
The patient's histopathology findings of mild hyperkeratosis accompanied by parakeratosis are consistent with Parakeratosis.
The patient's symptoms of pruritic papules are consistent with Psoriasis.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of well-developed cornoid lamellae with a decreased granular layer, individual cell dyskeratosis, and mild hyperkeratosis accompanied by parakeratosis are highly specific findings that align with Grover's disease, making it the most fitting diagnosis.
